steps.what: the count has no additive inverse -- the lack rung 4 repairs
steps.why: rung 1 hands up a COUNT (a chain length): a Nat. A count cannot be undone -- there is no n with n+1 = 0, because n+1 >= 1 > 0 always. This missing inverse is exactly what 'algebra' adds beyond 'number', and it is added below, not assumed.

steps.check: cross-add relation is refl/symm/trans over the sample
steps.determines: the integer is UNIQUE (as a class); its representative is CHOSEN
steps.expr: (a,b) ~ (c,d) iff a+d = c+b -- reflexive, symmetric, transitive
steps.what: an integer is a signed displacement; cross-add is an equivalence relation
steps.why: the pair (a,b) is a DIRECTION with magnitude ('a one way, b the other'), never a located thing. Sameness is same NET displacement, tested by cross-ADD so Nat's truncated subtraction (the is-not operation) is never invoked -- the positive form. Reflexive/symmetric/transitive make 'the integer' a genuine class, not an accident of the chosen pair.

steps.check: the (n,n) diagonal is exactly the class of 0
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the zero class is the whole diagonal)
steps.expr: the class of ZERO = { (n,n) : n:Nat } ; and (a,b) ~ 0 iff a = b

value.note: 0 names balance, not an object -- the counterpoint

steps.what: '0' is the counterpoint -- the balanced (diagonal) class, not a thing
steps.why: zero is not an object among the counts. It is the class of the BALANCED pairs (n,n) -- the diagonal a=b, where the two directions cancel to null displacement. It names BALANCE, the counterpoint, not a located thing (CORRECTIONS #2: 0 does not exist; it is the counterpoint). A pair sits at 0 exactly when its two directions are equal.

steps.check: +1,-1 distinct, inverse, and generate every class from 0
steps.expr: +1 := class(1,0) ; -1 := class(0,1) ; distinct, mutually inverse, and generating
steps.what: +1 and -1 are the two unit directions off the counterpoint
steps.why: +1 is one net step the defined way, -1 one net step the opposite way -- DIRECTIONS, not is/is-not. They are distinct (1+1 != 0+0), each other's inverse, and every integer is reached from the counterpoint 0 by iterating one direction or the other. This is what earns 'the number line': an origin and two directions.

steps.check: (a,b)+(b,a) ~ 0 for every pair in the sample
steps.determines: UNIQUE (each class has one inverse class)

value.inverse_is: the reversed direction (swap the two components)

steps.what: THE HEADLINE -- every integer has an additive inverse (its reversed direction)
steps.why: the one thing Nat lacked (4.1) is now supplied for EVERY element: reverse the direction (swap the components) and the sum balances to the counterpoint. The inverse of a direction IS the opposite direction; the two meet at 0. This is the whole content of 'algebra beyond counting', proved -- not assumed.

steps.check: add/neg representative-independent; embedding preserves +; rung-1 Nat embeds
steps.determines: UNIQUE (well-definedness makes the class operation unique)
steps.expr: addPair_congr, negPair_congr ; ofNatPair(a+b) = ofNatPair a + ofNatPair b (outright)

value.tie: thin, honest -- an available Nat, not a structural correspondence

steps.what: the operations are well-defined on the class; the count embeds, preserving +
steps.why: addition and negation do not depend on which representative is chosen -- the direction is a genuine property of the CLASS, so these are operations on integers, not on pairs. And counting sits inside as pure defined-direction displacement: n -> (n,0) preserves addition OUTRIGHT (definitionally, not merely up to ~). The tie to rung 1 is deliberately thin and honest: rung 1 produces a real Nat (a chain length) and that Nat embeds as (n,0) -- no rich structural correspondence is claimed.

steps.expr: identify(class(a,b)) := the net registration displacement; +1/-1 the two directions, 0 the counterpoint

value.reading: +1/-1 are the registration directions; 0 is the counterpoint

steps.what: the reading: this signed-displacement structure IS the floor's number line
steps.why: the mathematics above is unconditional. THIS step is the reading, held not proven: that the signed displacements ARE the floor's number line -- +1 and -1 the two directions a registration count can be extended in, 0 the counterpoint (not a thing). Kevin's floor note, now earned by the algebra but not derived from it. Capped as a postulate.

steps.determines: UNIQUE (well-definedness makes the class product unique)
steps.what: multiplication -- the ring core: a well-defined, commutative, distributive product
steps.why: the product of two signed displacements, kept in Nat ((ac+bd)-(ad+bc), no subtraction). Its HEADLINE is well-definedness -- multiplication is genuinely an operation on the CLASSES, not on pairs (mul_congr). With +1=(1,0) as the unit, commutativity, and distribution over addition, the integers become a commutative RING -- multiplication is real, derived from the same construction as the sum.

steps.check: order total & representative-independent; +/0/- trichotomy is EXACTLY one per integer
steps.determines: UNIQUE (a total order; the trichotomy is exhaustive and exclusive)
steps.expr: (a,b) <= (c,d) iff a+d <= c+b ; isPos(a,b) := b < a ; exactly one of +,0,- per integer
steps.what: the order and the ORIENTATION -- which direction is positive (trichotomy)
steps.why: the order is a total order on the classes (reflexive, total, representative-independent). Its content for the floor is the ORIENTATION: isPos says which of the two directions is positive (the +1 direction), and the TRICHOTOMY -- every integer is positive, the counterpoint 0, or negative, exactly one -- is precisely how the two directions and the counterpoint partition the number line. This is the orientation OWED by step 4.4's 'directions', now supplied.

steps.check: (p*q)*r ~ p*(q*r) over the sample; kernel proof mulPair_assoc
steps.what: associativity of the product -- the last ring axiom, now mechanised -- DERIVED
steps.why: the product is associative: distributing and reassociating the triple products puts both sides over the same eight degree-3 monomials, a linear identity. Verified exactly over the sample here, and PROVED in the kernel (mulPair_assoc) -- the commutative-ring structure is now complete, no ring axiom left owed.
